Anterior Composite Filling: Advice & Post-Operative Care
By Dr. Sakshi Jain
 Your anterior (front tooth) composite filling has been completed using a tooth-colored restorative material designed to restore the appearance, function, and strength of your tooth. Following these instructions will help ensure the longevity of your restoration.

Immediately After the Procedure
* If local anesthesia was administered, avoid biting your lips, cheeks, or tongue until the numbness completely wears off (usually 2–4 hours).
* Since composite fillings harden immediately with the curing light, you can generally eat once the numbness has subsided.
Eating & Drinking
* Avoid very hard foods (such as ice, hard candies, or nuts) on the treated tooth for the first 24 hours.
* Limit foods and beverages that may stain the restoration, such as coffee, tea, red wine, turmeric-rich foods, and tobacco products, especially during the first 24–48 hours.
* Maintain good hydration and rinse your mouth with water after consuming staining foods or drinks.
 Oral Hygiene

* Brush twice daily using a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste.
* Floss gently around the restored tooth every day.
* Good oral hygiene helps prevent decay around the edges of the filling and maintains its appearance.
* Mild sensitivity to hot, cold, or pressure is common for a few days and usually resolves on its own.

Mouth Guard – Protect Your Teeth and Smile

A mouth guard is a specially designed dental appliance that helps protect your teeth, gums, and jaw from injury and damage. It is commonly recommended for people who play sports, grind or clench their teeth while sleeping (a condition known as bruxism), or have jaw-related problems.

Sports activities can sometimes lead to accidental falls, collisions, or impacts that may cause broken teeth, cuts inside the mouth, or jaw injuries. Wearing a mouth guard acts like a protective cushion, reducing the risk of serious dental damage. It is especially important for children and adults who participate in contact sports such as football, basketball, hockey, cricket, and martial arts.

For patients who grind their teeth at night, a custom-made mouth guard can help prevent tooth wear, cracks, enamel damage, jaw pain, and headaches. It creates a protective barrier between the upper and lower teeth, reducing pressure on the teeth and jaw muscles.

At Dr. Sakshi Jain's Vital Dental Clinic, we provide custom-fitted mouth guards that are designed for comfort, durability, and maximum protection. Unlike over-the-counter options, custom mouth guards fit perfectly, allowing you to breathe and speak comfortably while wearing them.

Hard toothbrushing may seem like the best way to keep your teeth clean, but brushing too aggressively can actually harm your oral health. At Dr. Sakshi Jain Vital Dental Clinic, we often see patients with worn enamel, gum recession, and tooth sensitivity caused by excessive brushing pressure. Your teeth and gums need gentle care, not force.

Using a hard-bristled toothbrush or brushing with too much pressure can gradually damage the protective enamel layer of your teeth. Once enamel wears away, it does not grow back. This can lead to increased sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods. Hard brushing can also irritate and pull back the gums, exposing the tooth roots and increasing the risk of decay and discomfort.

Many people believe that if they brush harder, their teeth will become cleaner. In reality, proper technique matters far more than pressure. Dentists recommend using a soft-bristled toothbrush and brushing in gentle circular motions for two minutes twice a day. Holding the brush like a pen instead of gripping it tightly can also help reduce pressure.

Signs of hard toothbrushing include bleeding gums, tooth sensitivity, frayed toothbrush bristles, and receding gums. If you notice any of these symptoms, it is important to seek professional dental advice before the damage worsens.

At Dr. Sakshi Jain Vital Dental Clinic, we guide patients on correct brushing techniques and preventive dental care to protect their smile for years to come. Remember, gentle brushing is the

Periodontics is the branch of dentistry that focuses on the health of gums and supporting structures of the teeth. Healthy gums are very important because they help keep teeth strong and stable. Poor oral hygiene can lead to gum diseases such as gingivitis and periodontitis, which may cause bleeding gums, bad breath, pain, and even tooth loss if not treated on time.

The main goal of periodontics is prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of gum-related problems. Dentists advise patients to brush twice daily, floss regularly, and visit the dentist for professional cleaning to maintain healthy gums. Early signs of gum disease include redness, swelling, and bleeding while brushing. These symptoms should never be ignored.

Modern periodontal treatment includes scaling and root planing, gum surgery, laser therapy, and dental implants for replacing missing teeth. Dental implants have become a highly successful option because they provide both function and appearance similar to natural teeth.

Periodontics also plays an important role in overall health. Research shows that gum disease may be connected with diabetes, heart disease, and pregnancy complications. Therefore, maintaining good oral hygiene not only protects teeth but also supports general health and well-being.

Dr. Sakshi Jain believes that educating patients about gum care and regular dental check-ups can help prevent serious dental problems and improve quality of life.

🦷 Post Extraction Tips for a Smooth Recovery 🦷
By Dr. Sakshi Jain | Vital Dental Clinic

Getting a tooth removed can feel uncomfortable, but proper care after extraction helps you heal faster and avoid complications. Here are some simple and important tips to follow after your tooth extraction:

✅ Bite gently on the gauze pad for 30–45 minutes to control bleeding. Slight oozing is normal for a few hours.

✅ Avoid spitting, rinsing, or using a straw for the first 24 hours. This can disturb the blood clot and delay healing.

✅ Take prescribed medicines exactly as advised by your dentist. Do not skip painkillers or antibiotics if prescribed.

✅ Eat soft and cool foods like curd, khichdi, soup, smoothies, mashed potatoes, or ice cream. Avoid spicy, hot, crunchy, or hard foods for a few days.

✅ Apply an ice pack on the cheek for 10–15 minutes at a time to reduce swelling.

✅ Do not smoke or drink alcohol after extraction, as it slows healing and increases infection risk.

✅ Maintain oral hygiene carefully. Brush gently and avoid the extraction area for the first day. After 24 hours, rinse gently with warm salt water 2–3 times daily.

⚠️ Contact your dentist immediately if you experience severe pain, excessive bleeding, swelling, fever, or bad taste from the extraction site.

Your comfort and recovery matter to us. Follow these tips for a healthy and smooth healing process! 😊
